name: Multiple practitioners act as one on a shared operation
one_line: A group of practitioners designates one anchor whose own roll gates the whole collective attempt, with helper contributions computed by floor-division and conflicting personal commitments handled at two severities.

season_requires.need: Multiple independent actors must be able to jointly target the same single operation, with exactly ONE of them programmatically DESIGNATED as the operation's anchor via an explicit selection rule (highest value of a specific stat among those present), rather than by manual/GM choice.
season_requires.why: Without a rule-based designation, who leads a collective attempt would be an arbitrary GM call rather than a consistent, queryable game fact.

season_requires.need: All designated participants must roll the SAME gating step SIMULTANEOUSLY, with the ANCHOR's own individual result determining whether the COLLECTIVE structure forms at all, independent of how any helper's own roll came out.
season_requires.why: If any participant's success could substitute for the anchor's, the described asymmetric importance of the anchor role would be lost.

season_requires.need: If the anchor's roll fails, participants who individually succeeded on the SAME roll must still receive THEIR OWN individual outcome and consequences as if they had acted alone, rather than losing their result entirely.
season_requires.why: Without preserving individual results on anchor failure, a successful helper would be punished purely for the anchor's bad luck.

season_requires.need: Each helper's contribution to the anchor's pool must be computed as a FLOOR-DIVISION of one of the helper's own stats (that stat divided by 2, rounded down) added as bonus dice to the anchor, NOT as the helper's own separate independent dice pool.
season_requires.why: A separate pool per helper instead of a floor-division bonus to the anchor's own pool would produce a mathematically different, and much larger, collective result than the source specifies.

season_requires.need: A participant's own pre-existing personal commitment must be able to conflict with the operation's shared intent at (at minimum) two distinct severities, with different mechanical consequences per severity: a milder conflict silently disabling one property of that participant's dice, and a more severe, directly-opposing conflict requiring an ADDITIONAL pre-check roll whose failure removes the participant before the main roll occurs.
season_requires.why: A single conflict severity instead of two would erase the described distinction between a merely awkward alignment and a genuinely incompatible one.

season_requires.need: The system must support a single reusable comparison — whether the current collective pool falls below half of what the anchor could achieve alone — applying identically at TWO DIFFERENT MOMENTS in the operation's lifecycle (initial helper join/failure, and a later mid-operation contact drop), both triggering the same difficulty penalty when true.
season_requires.why: Implementing this as two separate ad hoc checks instead of one reusable comparison risks the two moments silently diverging in behavior.

season_requires.need: Any of the consequences that ordinarily fire once per solo operation must be able to SCALE their magnitude or count with the NUMBER of participants involved in a collective attempt, rather than firing identically regardless of party size.
season_requires.why: Fixed, party-size-independent consequences would understate the described proportionally greater effects of many configurations interacting at once.

season_requires.need: A SEPARATE variant of the collective-contribution structure must exist specifically for the highest-difficulty class of resolution actions, carrying its OWN difficulty ceiling that is higher than the standard structure's but explicitly caps out even against what would otherwise be additively-stacked collective bonuses.
season_requires.why: Without a hard ceiling that overrides additive stacking, a large enough group could trivialize the hardest resolution actions, contradicting the explicit cap.

temporal.span_seasons: n/a — resolves within a single scene/contact window
temporal.needs_memory_of: which participant is designated anchor; each participant's own commitment-conflict state; the running collective pool size, for the half-of-solo comparison.

who_acts: each participating practitioner (chooses to join, and individually rolls)
the anchor specifically (their roll gates the whole attempt)
GM/system (performs the anchor designation, the pool math, and the scaling of consequences)
knowledge: not primarily epistemic — the shared diagnosis step is explicitly described as all participants receiving the same description, i.e. no participant-specific information asymmetry within the collective attempt itself
ends_when: a roll resolves it (the shared gating roll, and any subsequent pre-check rolls) — the anchor designation and pool math are computation, not choices, though joining the collective attempt at all is a person-chooses step per participant.

name: A personal action interleaves with a mass-scale battle
one_line: A personal-scale action can be declared once per battle-turn inside a mass-scale resolution structure, with commanders forced to trade command capability for it, and the same underlying action's cost and timing scale differently at mass scale.

season_requires.need: A personal-scale action must be declarable and resolvable WITHIN a single unit of mass-scale time, strictly limited to a fixed maximum count per unit (here: one), rather than personal actions being either unavailable during mass-scale resolution or unlimited.
season_requires.why: Unlimited personal actions during mass combat would let a single character dominate a battle turn by turn; zero personal actions would erase the described zoom-in moments entirely.

season_requires.need: A named individual NPC becoming the target of a personal-scale action during mass combat must change that NPC's own tracked STATUS at the mass scale, distinct from any personal-scale state change to that NPC.
season_requires.why: Without a mass-scale status change, the personal duel would have no visible effect on the surrounding mass battle's own bookkeeping.

season_requires.need: An actor holding a mass-scale command role, upon choosing a personal-scale action, must have their mass-scale command capability for that SAME time-unit SUSPENDED — an explicit mutual exclusion between acting at the personal scale and exercising command at the mass scale in the same turn for the same actor.
season_requires.why: Without the suspension, a commander could act personally with no opportunity cost to their army, removing the described trade-off.

season_requires.need: The SAME action-category used at the personal scale elsewhere in the system must be usable DURING mass-scale resolution too, but its resolution TIMING must DIVERGE from its declaration timing, with the specific divergence (which later phase it resolves at) determined by WHICH SUB-TYPE was chosen at declaration.
season_requires.why: Without sub-type-dependent phase divergence, offensive and support uses of the same action would resolve identically, contradicting the described different phase assignments.

season_requires.need: That same action-category's resource-cost FORMULA must be swappable based on scale-context: multiplied by a fixed factor AND separately capped at a flat per-use ceiling specifically when invoked during mass-scale resolution, distinct from its ordinary personal-scale cost.
season_requires.why: A single fixed cost formula regardless of context would misprice the action relative to the described mass-scale multiplier-and-cap rule.

season_requires.need: A social-scale contest resolved BEFORE a mass-scale round's own declaration phase must be able to modify the STARTING mechanical state of that upcoming mass-scale round.
season_requires.why: Without cross-scale sequencing into starting state, a pre-battle appeal could not be represented as altering the battle it precedes.

season_requires.need: A mass-scale outcome (winning a qualifying engagement) must feed the SAME shared world-health currency used by the personal-scale action chains elsewhere in the system, as one of that currency's NAMED gain sources, alongside a scale-specific extra cost/tax applied when the same currency-spending action-category is used inside a mass-scale context.
season_requires.why: Without a shared-currency feed from mass-scale outcomes, the described convergence of personal and strategic play onto one common resource would not exist.

season_requires.need: The spatial resolution model during mass-scale combat must support a coarser zone-based movement abstraction, with a distinct cost rule for crossing between zones, separate from the personal-scale movement rules used outside mass combat.
season_requires.why: A single unified movement system regardless of scale would be unable to represent the described zone-based mass-combat spatial model distinct from ordinary personal-scale movement.

temporal.span_seasons: n/a — resolves within a single mass-combat encounter
temporal.needs_memory_of: which named NPCs are currently contested; which commanders have suspended command this turn; each declared operation's sub-type, for the phase-divergence.

who_acts: the commanding actor (choosing personal action vs. retaining command)
practitioners declaring Thread operations during mass combat
GM/system (resolves the phase-divergence and cost multiplication automatically once sub-type is declared)
ends_when: a person chooses it — each personal-scale action and command-suspension is a voluntary declaration; the phase-divergence and cost scaling are threshold/computation, not choices in themselves.

name: Two resolution modes collide over the same target
one_line: A roll-based personal-scale attempt and an order-based strategic-scale attempt targeting the same object with opposing intent are held and resolved together, with resource costs applying independent of who wins.

season_requires.need: Two structurally different resolution modes (a roll-based personal mode and an order-based strategic mode) must be able to target the SAME object with opposing intent, be DECLARED at different points in the same round, and be HELD without resolving until a single common later phase resolves them TOGETHER.
season_requires.why: Resolving each mode independently as it's declared instead of holding both for joint resolution would prevent the two from ever actually competing over the same outcome.

season_requires.need: The combined resolution of both modes' attempts must support THREE distinct outcome shapes: a margin-based comparison when both succeed, a straightforward win for whichever single side succeeded when only one does, and a 'neither effect happens' outcome when both fail — with the comparison rule needing to be a first-class computable relationship (net successes), not a GM call.
season_requires.why: Leaving the comparison to GM judgment instead of a computable margin rule would make the outcome of colliding orders unpredictable and unauditable.

season_requires.need: In ALL THREE outcome shapes, resource costs to the shared currency must be able to apply to the LOSING or FAILING side even though that side produced no narrative effect, such that the 'both fail' case can produce a pure net loss to the shared currency with no offsetting gain to any party.
season_requires.why: Coupling cost strictly to success would erase the described possibility of a mutual failure that still costs the world something, with nobody gaining.

season_requires.need: The resource changes to the shared currency arising from BOTH resolution modes in the same accounting step must be summed together and then capped by a single SEASONAL ceiling applied to the NET total after all sources for that season, not a per-event cap.
season_requires.why: A per-event cap instead of a seasonal net cap would allow unlimited currency swings within a single season as long as each individual event stayed under the cap.

season_requires.need: An individual character must be able to OPT IN to 'leading' an otherwise character-less strategic-mode action via an explicit declaration at a specific phase, and that declaration must determine whether an individual-character-scoped cost applies to that action instance AT ALL — absent the declaration, the action must proceed with NO individual-character cost attached.
season_requires.why: Without the opt-in default-free path, every strategic-mode order would either always or never carry a personal cost, losing the described player choice to personally lead (and personally pay for) a strategic action.

season_requires.need: A specific type of ongoing/recurring negative effect must be able to be REGISTERED against a specific spatial unit at one resolution phase while its actual per-period APPLICATION does not begin until a SEPARATE, later accounting step.
season_requires.why: Collapsing registration and activation into one atomic event would remove the described one-step delay before a newly-registered drift effect actually starts draining.

temporal.span_seasons: n/a — resolves within a single round's shared phase, though downstream drift effects persist across seasons
temporal.needs_memory_of: both modes' held, not-yet-resolved declarations until the shared phase; the running seasonal net total for the currency, for the cap; whether a leading character declared for a given strategic order.
temporal.needs_deadline: no — scoped to the round's shared resolution phase

who_acts: the personal-scale-acting character (declares their roll-based attempt)
the strategic-mode order's controller (declares the order, and optionally an individual leading character)
GM/system (resolves the shared phase, applies the seasonal cap, and registers the delayed recurring effect)
ends_when: a roll resolves it (the shared comparison phase) — the seasonal cap and the delayed-effect registration are threshold/computation rather than choices.
